title: The RAG Depth Setting: Semantic Search
use_cases: Configure when the AI loses track of intricate plot threads or specific character details
Implement when writing long-form narratives where earlier events are separated by large word counts
Use when balancing model intelligence with token cost efficiency
Adjust when writing complex scenes that require more than the default 5 historical references
content:
Here's where it gets interesting. The system doesn't send all your summaries to the AI every time you generate new text. That would be overwhelming.

Instead, it uses semantic search to find the most relevant summaries based on what you're currently writing.

The RAG Context Retrieval Depth setting controls how many summaries get retrieved. The default is 5 summaries, which works well for most stories.

Let's say you're writing chapter 20, and your protagonist returns to a location they visited in chapter 3. When you generate new text, the system searches your summaries for content related to that location and retrieves the chapter 3 summary, even though it's 50,000 words back.

The AI then receives:

- Your recent story text (last 4,000 characters)
- The 5 most relevant summaries from earlier chapters
- Your Author Notes (character profiles, world-building, plot notes)
- Any style preferences you've set

This gives the AI enough context to write coherently and reference earlier events without needing to process your entire manuscript every time.

If your story has intricate plot threads or you notice the AI forgetting details, you can increase the depth to 7 or 10 summaries. This sends more context but uses more tokens (and costs slightly more if you're using online models).

For most stories, the default of 5 works well.
